inputs_detail.derivation: Actuals ($M): Q1'25 95,300 (Q1'26 128.6B / 1.35), Q2'25 100,000 (Q2'26 143B / 1.43), Q3'25 106,900, Q4'25 119,100 (sum 421,300 vs Synergy FY2025 $419B, +0.5%); Q1'26 128,600, Q2'26 143,000, Q3'26 167,700. Forecast y/y: Q4'26 +52% (Q3 +55%, slight deceleration on a tougher Q4'25 base), 2027 +50/+47/+44/+40%, 2028 +35/+32/+30/+28%. Case: Big-4 capex rises 34.5% in 2027 and 29.3% in 2028 (NVDA model path) after ~+83% in 2026; capacity bought in 2026 lands in 2027 revenue, so growth stays above capex growth in 2027 and converges to it in 2028. Backlogs back it: AWS $578B, Microsoft RPO $677B (+73%), Google Cloud $561B. Alternatives: (a) market growth = Big-4 capex growth with no lag (2027 +34.5%, 2028 +29.3%): AWS FY2027 revenue ~-7%; (b) market holds the Q3'26 +55% through 2027: AWS FY2027 ~+5%.
inputs_detail.variant_view: A capacity-lag reading (revenue growth falling straight to capex growth in 2027) takes FY2027 AWS revenue ~7% lower, about -$5/share at the horizon.

inputs_detail.derivation: Actual capture = AWS revenue / Synergy market: Q1'25 30.7%, Q2'25 30.9%, Q3'25 30.9%, Q4'25 29.9%, Q1'26 29.2%, Q2'26 29.5%, Q3'26 27.4% (-3.5pt y/y). Forecast 27.0% Q4'26, then -0.3pt a quarter: 26.8/26.5/26.2/25.9% in 2027, 25.7/25.4/25.1/24.8% in 2028 (~1.2pt a year, a third of the last year's loss). Why slower than the last 4 quarters: Amazon's share of Big-4 capex is steady (~$220B of $750.7B = 29%) and its backlog doubled, so capacity, not demand, sets AWS's revenue; why still falling: Synergy names neoclouds and AI labs as eroding incumbents, Google Cloud grew 103% and Azure 48%. Alternatives: (a) capture held at Q3'26 27.4%: AWS FY2027 +~5% revenue; (b) the last year's -3.5pt/yr pace continues: AWS FY2027 revenue ~-6%; (c) Jassy's statement that AWS growth tops 40% in 2027 implies capture roughly flat with a ~45% market: +~4%.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Capture flat at 27.4% (Jassy's >40% AWS growth) adds ~$12/share; the full -3.5pt/yr pace takes ~$10/share off.

downside.story: P10: the cloud market slows toward Big-4 capex growth in 2027 (-10% to the market level) while AWS loses share faster (capture -5%), the depreciation wave takes AWS margin 3pt lower, Walmart takes retail-media share (NA margin -1.2pt), online retail grows ~2% slower, the market de-rates AMZN to ~21x like ORCL/GOOGL on negative FCF, and ANT falls 45% from $89.

base.story: Cloud market +45% in 2027 and +31% in 2028 as 2026 capacity lands; AWS grows ~35% in 2026-27 and ~26% in 2028 while capture slips ~1.2pt a year; AWS margin eases to ~36% on depreciation; NA grows with US online retail (~8%) and NA margin adds ~0.5pt a year; FY2028 EPS ~$11.5 (21% below the $14.58 consensus); 27x NTM EPS plus the Anthropic stake.

upside.story: P90: AWS growth holds near 40% (market +8%, capture +4%), GPU pricing keeps AWS margin ~2pt higher, ads re-accelerate (NA margin +0.8pt), the multiple re-rates 3 turns as FCF turns toward break-even, and ANT rises 40%.

reasoning: Rerun on post-Q3 data (all forecast sources published Sep 28-Nov 23). Lane (industry): the cloud market measured by Synergy grew 55% in Q3 2026 to $167.7B while AWS grew 39%, so AWS capture fell from 30.9% to 27.4% in a year; Google Cloud (+103%, backlog $561B) and Azure (+48%, RPO $677B) are the share takers, and Synergy names neoclouds. That makes AWS = market x capture, with the market's growth tied to the Big-4 capex path (NVDA model: $750.7B -> $1,009.45B -> $1,305.26B), giving AWS +35% in 2027 and +26% in 2028, below Jassy's >40% statement and UBS's 43%. Retail is built from Census e-commerce (Q3 +10.4%) with a small premium, trimmed because Walmart's US e-commerce (+23%) and ads (+37%) outgrow Amazon's ads (+11%). Margins: AWS eases with depreciation (UBS cut 2027 to 40%; we use ~37%), NA +0.5pt a year. Q4 FY2026 lands inside both guides (revenue at the midpoint, OI +2.7%) and below the record-adjusted figures; Q4 capex sits on the ~$220B guide (flagged). Our FY2027/28 EPS ($9.78/$11.51) is 8%/21% below consensus ($10.66/$14.58, MarketScreener 2026-11-20). Value: P/E leg, 27.0x (8-peer median 32.8x shrunk to AMZN's 25.7x, k=0.8) on our NTM EPS, plus the Anthropic stake, now listed (ANT $89.11; 14.7% after tax and a 15% lock-up discount = $14.6/share; cost ~$18B), less a 70%-weighted $3.2B Decart premium (reported by Calcalist/Globes, not signed as of today). Research target (12m) $321 (+24%); downside P10 $200 and upside P90 $414 move the cloud market, capture, AWS and NA margins, e-commerce, the multiple and ANT. Not driver-linked: the stake and the Decart adjustment. Research: ~35 queries/fetches; SEC refused scripted access, so filings were read with WebFetch; no option prices or implied volatility used.

downside.story: P10: the cloud market slows toward Big-4 capex growth in 2027 (-10% to the market level) while AWS loses share faster (capture -5%), the depreciation wave takes AWS margin 3pt lower, Walmart takes retail-media share (NA margin -1.2pt), online retail grows ~2% slower, the market de-rates AMZN to ~21x like ORCL/GOOGL on negative FCF, and ANT falls 45% from $89.

upside.story: P90: AWS growth holds near 40% (market +8%, capture +4%), GPU pricing keeps AWS margin ~2pt higher, ads re-accelerate (NA margin +0.8pt), the multiple re-rates 3 turns as FCF turns toward break-even, and ANT rises 40%.

model_inputs.structure_note: Quarterly driver-led set (16 quarters, 7 reported). Five drivers: Synergy cloud market x AWS capture x AWS margin builds AWS; Census US e-commerce x premium builds NA and International revenue (driven share 100%), with NA margin a driver and International margin a cited constant. The value is carried by one leg, P/E on the build's own GAAP NTM EPS at the horizon (Anthropic marks excluded, interest expense and interest income as their own lines) x a peer-shrunk 27.0x, plus the Anthropic stake (listed, after tax and a lock-up discount) and a probability-weighted Decart premium. No DCF leg (not a neocloud). No FCF-yield leg: AMZN is Consumer Discretionary, not in the tech FCF-leg list, and its FCF is negative in every projected year. SOTP shown only as a cross-check in fair_value.methods (weight 0).
model_inputs.gap_note: For Kilian: (1) Q4 FY2026 capex sits on the ~$220B FY2026 guide (guide_use declared): it moves only net debt and the research target by <0.5%. (2) Our FY2028 EBIT ($165.6B) is 16% below consensus ($197.2B) and FY2028 EPS (~$11.5) 21% below ($14.58): AWS share loss and the D&A wave; judgment, sized in the driver variant views. (3) The P/E peer median mixes cloud and retail peers; a cloud-only median (MSFT 26.7x, GOOGL 18.0x, ORCL 17.2x = 18.0x) would put the exit multiple near 21x, about -$65/share, and a retail-only median (WMT/COST/MELI/SE/SHOP 39.3x) ~31x, about +$45/share; we use the whole-company 8-peer median. (4) Decart below-20% financing questions: none; the deal is cash/stock and its share issuance would be <0.1%.
